# espalier — `.github/`

CI holds every push to the same three checks a release must pass: the test
suite, this repository's own `espalier lint`, and `build --check`. The
release procedure itself is `RELEASING.md`, written for the person running it.

## Project layout

    .github/
    ├─ workflows/      GitHub Actions workflows
    │  │
    │  ├─ ci.yml       the checks every push and pull request runs (required)
    │  │
    │  └─ release.yml  validating and publishing a GitHub release to npm
    │                  (required)
    │
    ├─ RELEASING.md    how a release is prepared and published (required)
    │
    └─ RELEASE-[major=0+].[minor=0+].[patch=0+].md
       one release's notes, published as its GitHub release (one or more
       matching files)

In `[major=0+]`, the text after `=` is a mask: each character matches one character of the name. `0` matches a digit. `+` repeats the element before it one or more times. `espalier help matching` has the full grammar.

## `RELEASING.md` — how a release is prepared and published

The checklist a release follows, from version bump to the published package.
A step that changes, such as a new file whose version must be bumped, changes
here in the same commit, because this page is what the next release is run
from.

## `RELEASE-[major=0+].[minor=0+].[patch=0+].md` — one release's notes, published as its GitHub release

Written for someone upgrading: what changed that they will notice, what they
must do about it, and what `espalier migrate` does for them. Opens with
`# Espalier <version>`. The file is the release body `gh release create
--notes-file` publishes, so it is written before the release is tagged and
not edited after it is published.

## `workflows/` — GitHub Actions workflows

### `ci.yml` — the checks every push and pull request runs

Runs on every supported Node version. It holds a push to what a release must
pass, so a release never discovers a failure CI could have reported.

### `release.yml` — validating and publishing a GitHub release to npm

Runs when a release is published. Validation repeats CI's checks on the
tagged commit and refuses a tag that does not match `package.json`; only
then does the publish job run, with npm trusted publishing and no token.
